paper.title: Arguments for The NOI Nanotransistor Affiliation to The FETs Family
paper.abstract: Among the nanodevices, the vacuum nanotransistors are intensively studied in the last decade. A recent novel device was proposed as the NOI - Nothing On Insulator - nanotransistor, inspired from ultrathin SOI devices. Therefore, this new device preserves some properties from the SOI structures. Obviously, the NOI nanotransistor is a vacuum tunnel device among the vacuum field emission devices. But the main target, in this paper, is to prove that its particularity comes from affiliation to the FETs family, monitoring the gate-control on the drain current. The drain current is activated by the VDS voltage under tunneling conditions. But the gate terminal modulates the carriers concentration and consequently the drain current flow, accordingly with its inherent included SOI structure. Also, a new model parameter comes to complete the NOI theory. The third order derivative was used for the extraction of a threshold drain-source voltage that splits the work domain in two conduction regions.

## Formalism Analysis

### Concept Complexity
**Topic:** Analytical and simulated arguments that the vacuum-channel NOI nanotransistor behaves as a field-effect transistor (gate modulation of carrier concentration), plus extraction of a threshold drain-source voltage via the third-order derivative.
**Level:** 2 (Low)
**Rationale:** The model is an approximation of the authors' earlier tunnelling model plus a standard first integration of Poisson's equation in a semiconductor film with an oxide boundary condition; Atlas simulations confirm the trend. This is the application of textbook device physics to a previously proposed structure, not a new mathematical model with independent validation.

### Formal Elements
- Definitions: 0
- Theorems: 0 (the "Non-Linear Electrical Conduction Theorem" is cited from [6], not stated or proved here)
- Proofs: 0
- Equations: 4

### Proportionality
Calculated complexity: 0
Expected range (Level 2): 0-15
Ratio: 0x upper bound

**Assessment:** Proportionate — the Fowler-Nordheim-style current expression, Poisson's equation, the VG-fS relation and the carrier-concentration expression are the physics the argument rests on.

### Issues
None identified in the formalism. The abstract states the aim "to prove" FET affiliation; what is offered is a qualitative accumulation argument and simulations, which is a weaker form of evidence than the wording implies.

---

## Citation Analysis

Nine of nineteen references include Ravariu or Rusu; all are on SOI/NOI devices or closely related device modelling, so none is judged irrelevant, but the ratio is excessive. In addition, references [3], [7], [8], [10] and [16]-[19] are papers from this journal or the authors' institution on unrelated topics (CMOS linearity, graphene capacitance, artificial-society simulators, UWB channel capacity, electro-thermal actuators), cited in bulk for generic statements such as "Usually the simulations help for a macro-model establishing, [16-19]" and "relationships with SOI devices, [6-10]". This looks like citation padding toward the venue and colleagues; reciprocal citation cannot be verified from the paper alone, so no ring flag is raised.

---

## Structural Analysis

Claims are supported by simulation figures and one numerical cross-check between Atlas concentrations and Eq. (4); there is no experimental device. The only acknowledged constraint is inline: model (1) "is acceptable in the VdsT vicinity". No code, simulation decks or data are offered.

---

## Conclusion

The technical content is modest but internally coherent and its formalism is proportionate. The paper's main weakness is citation conduct: a 47% self-citation ratio together with vague, bulk citations of unrelated journal papers.

paper.title: EMBG Resonators Based on Carbon Nanotubes for DNA Detection
paper.abstract: The paper presents modeling, fabrication and measurements of microwave propagation in electromagnetic band gap (EMBG) CNTs based resonator for DNA detection. We report on sensing of DNA wrapped on multi walled carbon nanotubes (CNTs) deposited over a coupled lines area of two types of EMBG resonator structures. A new EMBG structure with coupled lines as a defect in the structure in order to obtain a EMBG resonator is proposed. Two types of EMBG resonator structures having the distance between the coupled lines 50 µm and 100 µm respectively have been used in order to find the best coupling with CNTs. The transmission magnitude and the phase for two types of EMBG resonators based on carbon nanotubes has been presented. Detection of DNA using EMBG resonators based on CNTs was demonstrated by a shift of the resonance frequency and an averaged phase shift of 20 degrees for a broadband frequency range of 6-20 GHz.

artifact_assessment.evidence: no availability statement or link in the text

flag_details.NO_LIMITATIONS: No limitations section and no inline acknowledgment of constraints: a single DNA concentration, one sample per structure, no control for deposition thickness (which the paper itself invokes to explain the differing shifts) and no repeatability statistics are reported without caveat.

verdict.summary: Experimental microwave sensor paper with no formalism and clean citations, but a thin evidential base for its detection claim and no acknowledged limitations.

paper.title: CO2 Sensing Layers for SAW/BAW Devices
paper.abstract: The CO2 sensing performance of several coating layers deposited on piezoelectric devices (Surface and Bulk Acoustic wave - SAW/BAW) are discussed and compared. The layers are amino groups-based polymers and their selection was based on two principles: Hard Soft Acid Bases (HSAB) and Bronsted-Lowry. Experimentally measured CO2 frequency shifts and sensitivities of emeraldine, 4-sulfocalix[4]arene-doped polyaniline, matrix based emeraldine and carbonic anhydrase (PACA) are compared to previously reported results obtained for coatings such as: polyallylamine (PAA), polyethyleneimine (PEI), nanocomposite matrix based on PAA-aminocarbon nanotubes and PEI-aminocarbon nanotubes.

paper.title: A Continuous Chaos Generator Using Harmonic Oscillator Circuit
paper.abstract: This paper presents a continuous time chaos generator based on a simple oscillator structure. The developed mathematical model (based on dedicated software), Spice simulation and hardware implementation of the circuit demonstrate the strange attractor and chaotic behavior.

artifact_assessment.evidence: "The developed mathematical model (based on dedicated software)" - the software is mentioned but no availability statement or link is given

flag_details.NO_LIMITATIONS: No limitations section and no inline acknowledgment of constraints (e.g. sensitivity to component tolerances, the single swept parameter, or agreement between model and hardware); the conclusion is a single sentence.

verdict.summary: Circuit-level nonlinear-dynamics study whose ODE model, fixed-point analysis and Lyapunov estimates are all necessary; the paper is thinly referenced and states no limitations.

A technically sound, appropriately formal circuit study. Its weaknesses are structural: minimal literature context, no stated limitations and no released model code.

paper.title: Programmable Low Pass Filter Using the Gated Diode in Breakdown Collapse Regime
paper.abstract: In this paper we present a unity-gain follower amplifier based on a gated diode operated in breakdown regime in common cathode configuration. The amplifier has only one stage and it provides power amplification, high input impedance and a low output one. The maximum frequency that can be applied on the entrance of the amplifier so that the output remains undistorted is dependent on the bias current therefore it can be used also as a programmable low pass filter. The diode is fully characterized in order to set the bias in the linear region where the amplification is very close to one.

paper.title: Adjustable LDO with External Control Technique for Current Limit
paper.abstract: This paper presents an adjustable LDO with external control technique for the current limit. Using an external resistor, the user can change the current limit within wide domain. This is possible by using a special block which generates the current reference for the current protection block. The block consumes between 5 and 25 µA, and uses the 1.25 V voltage reference. The proposed LDO has a fast transient response and can deliver up to 300 mA continuous load current. It consumes 100 µA and has a dropout voltage of 200 mV at 300 mA.

paper.title: A Flexible Fabrication Process for RF MEMS Devices
paper.abstract: RF MEMS are assuming a great importance in the fast evolving telecommunication market and space applications. In the last years a flexible technology platform has been developed and continuously optimized at FBK (Italy) for the fabrication of RF MEMS basic components as well as complex RF circuits working in the frequency range from sub-GHz up to more than 100 GHz. The paper reports about the fabrication process and its capabilities. The most important process features are described together with some modifications required for the manufacturing of specific devices, like dielectric less RF MEMS switches. Examples of produced devices and their performances are briefly presented.

paper.title: Analytic and Electromagnetic Investigation of Millimeter Wave Membrane Supported CPWs Processed on High Resistivity Silicon
paper.abstract: This paper investigates a series of membrane supported millimeter wave transmission lines up to 110 GHz. The structures were fabricated using high resistivity silicon micromachining (wet etching). Three approaches, based on full-wave electromagnetic simulations, analytic closed form equations and equivalent circuit were used in the investigation process. The results were validated by the experimental results for different test structures. The analytic equations were inserted in a Matlab routine and the effective permittivity and characteristic impedance were plotted for various geometries. These same geometries were then simulated electromagnetically in CST Microwave Studio. A comparison between the two approaches is made. The effective permittivity of a membrane supported coplanar waveguide (CPW) line was extracted from measurements and it is in very good agreement with the electromagnetically simulated data.

artifact_assessment.evidence: "Formulas (1)-(3) were inserted in a Matlab routine" - the routine is described but no availability statement or link is given

verdict.summary: Solid comparative modelling study of membrane-supported CPWs to 110 GHz, validated against measurements, with standard closed-form equations, normal citation practice and candid inline discussion of discrepancies.

Calculated complexity: 0

One of ten references ([4], Neculoiu and Müller) is a self-citation (10%), relevant to the membrane technology used. Remaining references are standard textbooks and primary papers. No issues identified.

---

## Structural Analysis

Each modelling approach is compared against measurements on several test structures, and discrepancies are discussed inline: the analytic formulas' limitation on bulk silicon "can be observed especially for the effective permittivity curves", a persistent ~1.5 dB insertion-loss gap is attributed tentatively to dielectric-loss modelling, and S21 is noted to be "very sensitive to the calibration technique". The Matlab routine and measured S-parameters are not made available.

---

## Conclusion

The strongest paper in the issue on structural grounds: proportionate formalism, clean citations, multi-method validation and honest treatment of residual disagreement. Reproducibility would benefit from released data and code.

paper.title: Operating Frequency Extension of Surface Assembled Microwave Components
paper.abstract: A novel transition from microstrip and coplanar lines to the specific signal interfaces of usual surface assembled components is considered in this paper. It is aimed to improve the bandwidth of printed circuit board (PCB) based packages, provided by smaller values and better geometry controlled parasitic elements due to proposed structure. Moreover, the same interface model is compatible with surface assembly of substrate integrated waveguide components. Guidelines for component values preliminary calculation and optimization are presented. Microstrip test circuits were accordingly manufactured for design verification, with satisfactory results up to 8 GHz. The relative permittivity of FR-4 substrate material used in our experiments is considered the solely responsible for certain differences existing between simulated and experimental data, because they became effective after PCB manufacturer was replaced.

artifact_assessment.evidence: no availability statement or link in the text

verdict.summary: Proposal of a circularly symmetric via transition for surface-mounted microwave components using standard closed-form design equations; the experimental verification is limited and its mismatch with simulation is attributed to a single cause without testing.

## Citation Analysis

Two of eleven references ([7] and [11]) are by the author (18%), both on the same transition/SIW work and relevant. Two references are web pages (Wikipedia, a vendor product page). Self-citation is moderately elevated but below 20%.

---

## Structural Analysis

The paper acknowledges a shortcoming of the transition inline (the connection "can be only performed with transitions from stripline") and states that measured results "are not yet in very good agreement with circuit simulations". However, the discrepancy is declared "solely" due to FR-4 permittivity tolerance without any permittivity measurement or re-simulation to test this. Experimental evidence is a few microstrip test structures; the SIW part is argued by reference to other work. No data or design files are offered.

---

## Conclusion

A reasonable engineering proposal with appropriate formalism and acceptable citation practice, whose experimental support is preliminary and whose explanation of the simulation-measurement gap is asserted rather than demonstrated.
